text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Kenneth Matiba, chairman of opposition party FORD-Asili, dispels rumours that he had been injured under mysterious circumstances, but says Kenyans should hold the government responsible should anything happen to him.

- The High Court in Mombasa is told by the ruling Kenya African National Union (KANU) party that the president cannot be sued while still in office as he enjoys immunity from any civic or criminal proceeding.

- A minister of state in the office of the president, Jackson Kalweo, denies reports that the government put opposition leaders under house arrest on June 1, saying that the leaders opted to lock themselves in their homes.
- One policeman died and three others were injured after the patrol car in which they were chasing a suspected thief crashed into a bus in Nairobi.
- Islamic leaders from the mainly Moslem town of Mombasa demand the immediate and unconditional restoration of Sheikh Khalid Balala's Kenyan citizenship.
- "No reform, no budget," say constitutional reform activists who threaten to storm into Parliament on the budget day, June 19, to press for constitutional change.
- Sharp differences emerge between key planners calling for constitutional reforms ahead of nationwide rallies scheduled for June 21.
- The Dutch ambassador to Kenya calls on Kenyan politicians to promote dialogue and the rule of law.
- Questions are being raised over last week's car accident which cabinet minister Simeon Nyachae miraculously survived.
